styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a tiny red/pink stool, smaller than one 16x16 tile, with only 7 distinct colours in total. It shows about 3 tones: a lighter top, a mid body, and a darker base or outline. The references (bench, hedge, stall, well) carry 5-6 steps per material, with grain, per-element highlights and texture dots. The stool has no visible grain, speckle or per-part highlight, so its small surfaces read as flat fills even though no 5x5 block is measured flat. Only 4% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline is tinted (dark red-brown) and not a black sticker line. That is a point in its favour, but the shading is shallow and the form is simple. Next to the bench, which has wood grain and slat shading, it looks thinner and flatter. The density facts cannot be used because the piece is under one tile, but by eye it is clearly less rich than the references.
